Given my preferences (w > y > x > z) and priorities (w:1, x:2, y:1, z:2), and the information that most applicants prefer y > x > w > z, I need to consider a strategic ranking.

If I rank w as my first choice, it's likely many others will *also* rank w highly. However, w only has a priority of 1 for me, and competition will be fierce. Given most applicants prefer y, and y also has a priority of 1 for me, ranking y first might be a better strategy. This increases my chances of matching to a school I like, as y may have more available spots due to lower overall demand compared to w.

Ranking y first also doesn't significantly hurt my chances at w. If w has space after matching higher-priority applicants, I could still get in. Ranking x and z as my last choices aligns with my preferences and won't likely improve my chances at any school.

Therefore, I will rank y as my first choice, hoping to capitalize on its relatively lower demand despite its high preference for me.
